$comment: The mapping set for the Sheffield PGT form, DRAFT, one file for the whole blueprint (a plan reads one set).
Authored from Vahid's words. Since 2026-09-16 (ADR-0118) the signature is his alone, and a set signed by its
author admits his own account and nothing else; a second person's review is a precondition of serving a real
student. Not usable until signed, and not executable until every required field is mapped.
Equal opportunities (page9), 2026-09-11, ADR-0102 and Vahid's correction from the live dropdown: both values
are 'Prefer not to say'. The disability refusal COVERS the eleven other controls of the same question. The
ethnic-origin refusal quotes nothing: the field's captured text says nothing about a later opportunity.
Personal (page3) and contact (page4), P89: mapped as far as the profile registry reaches. Date of birth is
three selects, rendered with the D / MMMM / YYYY patterns. The e-mail is asked twice and mapped twice. The
country select takes the portal's own upper-case names; the option map here is PARTIAL — eight countries
whose names the capture shows — and a student from any other refuses to render (render_refused) rather
than being approximated. The reviewer extends it from the captured option list, never from memory.
NOT mapped, and why: employment (page8) asks four required fields — start date, position, employer,
duties — for which the profile registry has no field. A registry addition is a product decision (what the
profile collects), raised in P89, not made here. Every optional field without a mapping is passed over.
Registration (page0), P91, from the signed-out read of the entry page: the e-mail from the profile; the two
password fields as secure_credential for portal_account_creation, filled by the Secure Plane from a value
nothing else holds, which checkUsable requires of any password field (ADR-0043).

Education (page7), P98: the page repeats over education.prior_qualifications (ADR-0104). Its six document slots are student handoffs — the student attaches them, and the preview says so under each qualification. No field on it is mapped yet: the registry's Qualification has level, subject, institution, countryCode, completionYear, grade and gradeScale, and which portal box each fills waits on the reviewer.

P100 (ADR-0105): the six status radios beside the education page's slots are handed to the student with their slots — 'My transcript is in English' is the student answering the question the slot asks. The subject list is loaded by pressing subjectSearchButton after typing subjectSearch (the dependencies read names the control: onclick searchSubjects()); the press is recorded on the field, not mapped.

Education (page7), ADR-0107 (2026-09-12): the six status radios are no longer handed to the student — a companion is mapped by nothing. When the radio's option values are read from a copy of the fieldset markup, the blueprint names each slot's defer option (whenDeferred) and its 'not providing' option (whenNotProviding); until then the slots are the student's act on a page nothing fills, which is admitted.

Education (page7), P108 (2026-09-12): the six Documentary Evidence radios' values are now in the blueprint (0.2.12) from Vahid's reading of the live page — whenAttached Uploaded, whenDeferred UploadLater, whenNotProviding NotSending on every slot; NotRequired is the fourth value and is named by nothing. With the defer value named, the page is NO LONGER one that nothing fills: each qualification's six radios are set to UploadLater by the runner while the qualification's own fields (institution, degree, subject, dates, grade) still wait on the reviewer. DO NOT SIGN this set while that is so — a run would save a qualification that says only 'later' six times. The certificate slot's companion is paired with certificateStatus from the file input's own handler (onchange ticks certificateUploadRadio, the id of that group's Uploaded option), not from the name; the radio's copy says 'proof of registration', so what the slot IS is Iman's to settle from the page (README, P108).

Language (page6), P109 (2026-09-12): the certificate group's values are in the blueprint (0.2.13) from Vahid's live reading — Uploaded / UploadLater / NotSending / NotRequired, the same shape as education — and its companion names the three; previousEnglishEducation submits Yes / No. Nothing on this page is mapped, so its companion is left as the form has it. NotRequired here reads 'We do not require a certificate to be uploaded if you are a UK appl[icant]…' — a claim about who the applicant is: the third distinct meaning of that one token on this form, and never ours to choose. Twenty-three radio groups on personal, contact and nationality still carry the capture's element ids as values; no mapping names one, and none may until each page is read the same way.

Personal, contact, nationality (pages 3-5), P110 (2026-09-12): every radio group's values are now in the blueprint (0.2.14) from Vahid's reading with the snippet. The yes-or-no groups do NOT agree on case across the form — personal.do submits Yes / No, nationality.do yes / no — so a constant on one must carry that page's case exactly; the runner sets a radio by value and normalises nothing. corrContactDateType: the value 'After' is shown as 'From this date:' and 'Before' as 'To this date:' — map from the text beside the value, never from the value alone. The five nationality document slots still carry no companion: their groups' values are known (Uploaded / UploadLater / NotSending, no NotRequired) but the slot-to-group pairing waits on the file inputs' own handler markup, which Vahid offered to read.

Nationality (page5), P111 (2026-09-13): each of the five file inputs carries onchange: document.getElementById('<slot>UploadRadio').checked=true, and no radio on the page carried such an id when Vahid read it. The handler names the intent; the DOM as read does not show which group the id belongs to, and if it belongs to nothing the handler throws and the page ticks nothing on attach. The five companions stay out of the blueprint until one more reading settles which (README, P111). When they go in, the runner needs only the group's name and the value Uploaded — both read — not the id.

Nationality (page5), P112 (2026-09-13): the five document slots are NOT on an international student's path. showHideDocumentUploads(), read by Vahid from the live page, shows each upload only on a claim of UK status — a British passport, indefinite leave, marriage to a UK citizen, refugee status — and with nationality and residence set to Iran none appeared. The blueprint (0.2.15) carries visibleWhen on four of the five file inputs from the function's own reads (yes on britishPassport / indefinateVisa / spouseOfUKCitizen / refugeeStatus); utilityBillScan is shown on britishPassport OR indefinateVisa, which the condition vocabulary cannot say, so it carries none and the plan treats it as an optional unmapped field, passed over. No slot on this page is to be mapped for an international student; a document mapped to one would be attached into a hidden block. The five companions are moot for the path and stay out.

Education (page7), P113 (2026-09-13): the repeating page's listing is named (ADR-0106) from Vahid's read of summary.do with two qualifications saved — each entry's heading is an h5 reading exactly 'Previous Education N' inside div.homepageInfomation (misspelled on the page; kept as written) inside div.homepageBlock, both wrappers shared by every section. The entry locator is text-shaped by necessity — the structure counts sections — and exact to the number: h5:text-matches('^Previous Education [0-9]+$'). A qualification is saved when that count grows by one.

Contact (page4), P116 (2026-09-13): the UK postcode is two boxes — corrPostcode and corrPostcode2 both came back from Vahid's read-back, three characters each for his — so the single-value mapping was wrong and is replaced by the uk_postcode format on each box, split at the postcode's own seam (inward = last three, outward = the rest), never at 3+3. Nothing on this page was normalised by the portal: e-mail, address, town and postcode came back exactly as typed, case included. The permanent-address fields (perm*) stay unmapped, as before.

Education (page7), P118 (2026-09-13, ADR-0109): a mapping to a typeahead names the VALUE the form submits, and the blueprint records what each value reads as. The institution box (institution-ts-control) now carries the eleven entries Vahid read for 'Sheff' with the United Kingdom chosen — the two 'Sheffield International College' entries are SCH40484 and SHE0512 — and its escape by value, 'Not in list', whose value is its own label. No mapping to the box is authored: a qualification's institution is a free-text profile part, and a mapping must reach the box through an option rule onto these entries (partial, like the country map), which is the reviewer's to write; a student whose institution is not among them is a handoff, never the escape. The country box's entries are the captured <select>'s and are recorded on the box when it is mapped.

Employment (page8), P129 (2026-09-14, ADR-0111): the registry now holds employment.history — decided by Vahid: 'employment goes into the registry as a new group' — and the page repeats over it, as education does. The four required fields and the start year and end date are mapped per job: the start month by the select's English names, the year as digits, the end date left EMPTY for a job the student said is current (part … absent: leave_empty — their statement, not our inference), the employer's name and address joined into the one textarea, the duties verbatim. A student who confirmed NO jobs fills the page zero times and the preview says so; a student never asked stays unavailable and blocks. The listing on summary.do for a saved job (ADR-0106's `recorded`) waits on Vahid's read with one throwaway job saved; until then every employment item is uncertain at the save.

Employment (page8), P130 (2026-09-14): the listing is named (ADR-0106) from Vahid's read of summary.do with one throwaway job saved — the heading reads exactly 'Previous Employment 1', the same shape as education's, so the entry locator is the same shape: h5:text-matches('^Previous Employment [0-9]+$') inside div.homepageInfomation. The wrapper is education's, on his word that the shape is the same; the capture's HTML is not in the commit. The summary lists a job's start date, end date, title and employer, and NOT its duties; under ADR-0106 §2 a per-item page is counted, never read back by value, so nothing confirms a saved job's values today, and a listing read-back could never reach duties.

Education (page7), P132 (2026-09-14): the dependent lists are in the blueprint (0.2.21) from Vahid's read of the page AS IT STOOD (--as-is) with United Kingdom, University of Sheffield and the grading system 'UK Bachelors Degree (BA, BSc)' chosen and 'business' searched: institutionCode holds the chosen value SHEFFIELD (the same value P118's typeahead entry carries); gradingSystemId's six options with numeric values (7, 8, 9, 81) and the escape 'Not in list', PER INSTITUTION — Sheffield's; grade's nine for system 7 — 1st, 2.1, 2.2, 3rd, Pass, Fail and the two non-grades 'Still waiting for grade' / 'Failed to complete course' — PER GRADING SYSTEM; subject's 87 for one search word, two values with a trailing space the label hides and one value listed twice. No mapping on this page is authored here: the registry's Qualification has a completion year and no start or end date, and the page's four date selects are marked mandatory — raised as blocker 27, his decision, the same shape as item 2 was. degree and unlistedDegree keep the third read's marks; the as-is read did not see the row's star, and the difference is flagged for the reviewer.

Education (page7), P134 (2026-09-15, ADR-0112): Qualification now carries a start and an end as month and year and an optional award date — decided by Vahid: 'add the dates to Qualification. Same reasoning as employment.' The six date selects are mapped per qualification: the start and end months by the selects' three-letter names, the years as digits, the award date left EMPTY when the student has none (part … absent: leave_empty — an absent award claims nothing) and never derived from the end. The page's other fields (institution, degree, subject, grading system, grade) still wait on the reviewer's option maps onto the observed lists (P132) and on blocker 25.

Nationality and residence (page5), P139 (2026-09-15, ADR-0115): the three registry groups Vahid confirmed — residence (the country of permanent residence, in the UK now, the entry date as MONTH AND YEAR by his change, a history of periods, three asked booleans), immigration.uk_status (seven claims, all asked, none derived) and immigration.uk_study (none, or studied with its details). Thirty-six mappings: the residence selects and radios, the entry date's month and year, the four previous-country blocks from the first four periods of the history (empty beyond what the student listed; the to-date empty for a current period), the seven status radios, and previousStudentVisa from the study's kind. Deliberately unmapped: every DAY select (the profile holds no day — a day the portal insists on is asked of the student as any unavailable value), ukPermanentResidence (a UK region the registry does not hold; not on an international student's path), and the UK-study block shown after 'yes', which waits on the page's show/hide script from Vahid's committed markup. The country maps are PARTIAL (eight countries), for the reviewer to extend from the captured options.

Nationality (page5), P141 (2026-09-15, ADR-0117): the passport is one value, held or stated as none — decided by Vahid: 'a student who does not have a thing has three empty values and nothing anywhere saying why. Fold them.' passportNumber maps the held number through part → number, and for none types the portal's own instruction, quoted from the row's tooltip into this set through absent: { typed: 'no passport' } — the important half, in his words: the portal's words live in the reviewed mapping and never in the profile; the tempting shortcut of storing the string once and reusing it everywhere is refused.

Nationality (page5), P142 (2026-09-15): nationality.js read from Vahid's commit. Two registry fields renamed once, from the script: residence.always_in_residence_country and residence.outside_residence_country_last_three_years — the page fills both questions with the permanent-residence country's name, 'the UK' only when that is the United Kingdom. Nine mappings added: fundingNationality and countryOfBirth (partial, keyed on ISO codes; the registry's nationality vocabulary flagged), and the UK-study block after 'yes' — the level in the registry's closed words, the 'Other' text, the years and months on the visa, the visa expiry's day, month (the select's own spellings through an option map after the month's name) and year. The five per-level qualification selects stay unmapped: the portal's own list against the student's free-text qualification, blocker 25's shape. The draft (0.2.22) now carries the page's sections with the script's show/hide as visibleWhen; a mapped field the page hides is neither typed nor missing.

P143 (2026-09-15): no mapping changed. The note on livingInUK now says that the page answers the question itself when living-outside is 'no' — a value the student never gives — so a reviewer or a later phase does not read that box as the student's answer.

The year options are four-digit years.

Town / City:*
Country:* — the portal's own upper-case names as values. PARTIAL map; any other country refuses to render, for the reviewer to extend from the captured options.

UK Post Code: (* UK only) — the FIRST of two boxes (maxlength 4), shown when the country is the United Kingdom. The outward code, split at the postcode's own seam (P116: Vahid's read-back showed two boxes, and 'must not assume 3+3'). The portal stores it as typed, case included.
The SECOND UK postcode box (maxlength 4): the inward code — a digit and two letters, always three characters. Hidden with the first when the country is not the United Kingdom.

The international postcode box, shown when the country is not the United Kingdom. Both boxes carry the same part; the plan honours the blueprint's visibleWhen (P90), so only the box the form shows is filled.
Start Date:* — the month select's values are the English names, 'January'…'December'; the entry's start month (1–12) maps onto them. Per job (the page repeats over employment.history, ADR-0111).
The year select's values are the four digits. Unstarred on the page; mapped because a start month without its year is not a start date.
End Date: — optional on the page. Left EMPTY for a job the student said is current (end.kind = current has no date): their statement, never a blank we inferred (ADR-0111).
As endMonth.
Job Title / Position held:* — maxlength 200 on the page.
Name and address of employer:* — one textarea; the entry holds them apart and they are joined here, the name on the first line, the address as the student gave it after it.
Brief Overview of Duties(Max 4000 characters):* — the student's own words, verbatim. The 4,000 cap is the page's; nothing here trims.

source.rationale: Health is Article 9 data this system does not hold. The form's own 'Prefer not to say' is ticked: a stated refusal to route the answer through AskiMate, not the student's answer. The empty save is refused (Vahid, 2026-09-11), so a refusal the form offers is the only honest entry.

mappings.note: Country of permanent residence — the portal's own values, with their ':H'/':O' suffix as captured. PARTIAL map (eight countries), as the contact page's; any other refuses to render, for the reviewer to extend from the captured options. A statement, not the address's country (ADR-0115).

Are you currently living in the UK?* — asked, never read off the history (ADR-0115). Typed only when the page shows the question: after 'yes' to living outside the country of permanent residence. When that answer is 'no', nationality.js hides this question and ticks it ITSELF from the residence (yes for United Kingdom:H, no otherwise): a box whose value the student never gives and this system never types — a read-back of it is the portal's inference, not the student's statement (Vahid, 2026-09-15; P143). The page's lower-case yes/no (P110).
Inside/Outside UK — the same fact as livingInUK, in the portal's other words.

Have you been living outside of <country of permanent residence> during the last 3 years?* — the span is filled by the page's script with that country's name (the UK only when it is the UK). Asked, not computed from the history. Vahid: 'The history is what they remembered; the answer is what they claim.' Renamed once from the script (P142).

Have you always lived in the <country of permanent residence>?* — the span is filled by the page's script with that country's name (the UK only when it is the UK); asked, not computed (ADR-0115; renamed once from the script, P142). Shown only to a resident of the UK or its territories.
Have you always lived in the EU?* — asked, not computed (ADR-0115).

Do you have a British passport?* — the student's own claim, never derived from the passport's issuing country. Vahid: 'a wrong yes opens a document slot the student must refuse or fill.' Lower-case yes/no (P110).

Do you have indefinite leave to enter or remain in the UK?* — the student's own claim, never derived from the passport's issuing country. Vahid: 'a wrong yes opens a document slot the student must refuse or fill.' Lower-case yes/no (P110).

Do you hold refugee status?* — the student's own claim, never derived from the passport's issuing country. Vahid: 'a wrong yes opens a document slot the student must refuse or fill.' Lower-case yes/no (P110).

Are you a migrant worker?* — the student's own claim, never derived from the passport's issuing country. Vahid: 'a wrong yes opens a document slot the student must refuse or fill.' Lower-case yes/no (P110).

Are you the spouse/civil partner of a UK citizen?* — the student's own claim, never derived from the passport's issuing country. Vahid: 'a wrong yes opens a document slot the student must refuse or fill.' Lower-case yes/no (P110).

Do you have an EU passport?* — the student's own claim, never derived from the passport's issuing country. Vahid: 'a wrong yes opens a document slot the student must refuse or fill.' Lower-case yes/no (P110).

Are you the spouse/civil partner of an EU citizen?* — the student's own claim, never derived from the passport's issuing country. Vahid: 'a wrong yes opens a document slot the student must refuse or fill.' Lower-case yes/no (P110).

Have you previously studied in the UK?* — from the kind of immigration.uk_study: 'none' is a statement (ADR-0113). The block the page shows after 'yes' (qualificationLevel, the five per-level selects, highestQualificationOther, years/months on the visa, the visa expiry) is NOT mapped in this set: the draft has no visibleWhen for it, and mapping a hidden select would type into a box the page does not show. Its show/hide is read off the page's own script from Vahid's committed nationality.do markup, as P112 read showHideDocumentUploads, before those mappings are written.

Please enter your passport number below. This is required in order to comply with UK immigration law.* — the number of a held passport, verbatim (thirty characters at most on the page). For a student who has STATED they have no passport (identity.passport kind = none), the portal's OWN instruction is typed, quoted from the row's tooltip: "If you don't have a passport please enter 'no passport' in the box." The words live here, in the reviewed mapping, and never in the profile (ADR-0117): they are Sheffield's instruction, not a fact about the student, and a portal that says something else gets its own words.

Nationality — the portal's own ISO-code values with their ':H'/':E'/':O'/':Q' suffix, which the page's script reads to decide which sections to show. PARTIAL map (eight), keyed on ISO codes as every country map in this set is; the registry's identity.nationality has no fixed vocabulary yet (the passport plan reads the word off the document, the interview asks 'a nationality or country'), which is flagged for the reviewer and for Vahid — a map by rule needs one.
Country of birth — the same select as the nationality's; PARTIAL map, the same caveat on the registry's vocabulary.

What is the highest qualification level you have studied in the United Kingdom?* — the study's level in the registry's closed words onto the portal's; empty (and hidden by the page) for a study of kind 'none'. Shown after 'yes' to previous study in the UK (P142, from nationality.js).

Please provide details of the qualification — the qualification in the student's words; shown only for the level 'Other'. The five per-level selects are NOT mapped: they need the student's qualification in the portal's own list (UG DEGREE, MASTERS, …), which the registry's free-text qualification cannot name by rule — the same shape as blocker 25's institution box; flagged for Vahid.
Years on the student visa — from timeOnVisa; empty when the study carries none. The page refuses a save with 0 years and 0 months (validate()).
Months on the student visa — as the years.
If you are currently studying in the UK, the current visa's expiry — a full date, read off the visa; empty when the study carries none. The day, as digits.
The month, in the select's own spellings (Jan … June, July … Sept …) through an option map after the month's name (P142).
The year, as digits — the select holds 2026 to 2030 only; a later expiry refuses to render rather than choosing the nearest.
